name: Machine Chest Press
description: The machine chest press is a guided horizontal pressing exercise performed on a dedicated chest press machine. The fixed movement path reduces the stabilization demand compared to free-weight pressing, allowing lifters to focus attention on pectoral contraction or to safely train to or near muscular failure without a spotter. It is an effective tool for hypertrophy, beginners, and individuals returning from injury.

execution.starting_position: Sit in the chest press machine with the back flat against the pad. Adjust the seat height so the handles are at mid-chest level. Grip the handles with an overhand grip, elbows bent and in line with the hands.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust the seat height so handles align with mid-chest. Set the starting position pin if available so you don't have to reach back awkwardly to initiate. Select weight.
steps: Step 1: Sit with back firmly against the pad, feet flat on the floor. Grip handles at chest level.
Step 2: Brace the core and retract the shoulder blades slightly against the pad.
Step 3: Exhale and press the handles forward until the arms are fully extended but not locked out.
Step 4: Inhale and slowly return the handles to the starting position, feeling a stretch across the chest.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the press; inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Allowing the lower back to arch away from the pad during the press
Fully locking out the elbows aggressively at full extension
safety_considerations: Use the machine's start-pin or lever to initiate the rep safely without shoulder strain
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Return fully to feel a chest stretch on each rep; press to near full extension without hyperextending.
coaching_cues: Press your back into the seat throughout — don't let it peel away
Think about squeezing the pecs together as you extend
